newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian survey finds information overload.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian survey finds information overload.

text.p: A survey of Australian, British, U.S. and Asian managers has found that about two-thirds are so stressed because of information overload that their social lives and health are affected.
The survey of 1,300 managers by Reuters Business Information found that 62 percent of Australian managers suffered ill-health as a direct result of dealing with excessive information.

"Sixty-nine percent of Australian managers testify that their personal relationships suffer due to information overload," Reuters Business Information said in the report, titled "Dying for Information".
The survey also found that 66 percent of Australian managers reported tension with work colleagues arose because of stress associated with information overload.
"Fifty two percent of Australian managers either often or very frequently work late or take work home as a result of having to deal with too much information," Reuters Business Information said.
"Senior managers in Australia are more typical of their Asian counterparts with only nine percent reporting that they frequently stay late," it said.

A third of Australian managers said they believed their colleagues wasted too much time collecting information while two thirds believed the cost of gathering information exceeded its value to the business.
